newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand sets baht midrate at 6-1/2 yr low.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand sets baht midrate at 6-1/2 yr low.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Wednesday set the baht/dollar midrate at 25.86, the lowest level since June 1990, a central bank official said.
The baht has been weakening steadily against the dollar, which has continued its relentless climb against the majors.
The greenback surged to its highest level in almost four years against the Japanese yen in overnight trade.

"Thailand will not do anything about the baht's easing against the dollar because we think the volatility will be short-term, and it is caused by external factors," central bank spokeswoman Duangmani Vongprathip told Reuters.
The dollar is believed to have the heaviest weighting in the basket of currencies with which the Bank of Thailand sets a daily midrate for the local currency.
The midrate was set at 25.81 on Tuesday.
